title: Timers and Browser Scheduling
summary: Schedule work without assuming it runs at an exact time.
nestedConcepts: Schedule visual work before a repaint

subtopics.title: Schedule one callback with setTimeout()
subtopics.explanation: `setTimeout()` asks the browser to run a callback after at least the requested delay. It is not an exact clock: a busy page or background tab can make it run later. Use it for a delayed action, not for measuring precise elapsed time.

subtopics.title: Repeat work with setInterval()
subtopics.explanation: `setInterval()` schedules a callback repeatedly until you clear its timer. If a callback takes longer than the interval, work can overlap or drift. For polling that must wait for each request to finish, schedule the next timeout after the current work completes.

subtopics.title: Schedule visual work before a repaint
subtopics.explanation: `requestAnimationFrame()` asks the browser to run a callback before it paints the next frame. Use it to update an animation in step with display refresh, rather than using a short interval. Cancel the request when the animation ends or its component is removed.

subtopics.title: Understand the microtask queue
subtopics.explanation: Promise callbacks and `queueMicrotask()` run after the current JavaScript task finishes and before the browser takes another task. A large chain of microtasks can delay rendering and input. Yield back to the browser when repeated work should not block the page.

subtopics.title: Clean up scheduled work
subtopics.explanation: Keep the timer or animation-frame ID so you can cancel work when it is no longer needed. In a React effect, clear the timeout or interval in the cleanup function. This prevents stale callbacks from updating a screen after its component has unmounted.

foundations.overview: Timers ask the browser to run a callback later. setTimeout does not guarantee an exact deadline; busy work can delay it. requestAnimationFrame schedules visual updates before a paint. queueMicrotask runs after the current task and before the next rendering opportunity.
foundations.mentalModel: A timer is a place in line, not an alarm that stops everything else.
foundations.whyItMatters: Understanding the queues helps avoid frozen screens and unexpected ordering.

keyTakeaways: Microtasks run before the browser takes the next task.
Clear timers when their owner is no longer needed.
